name: Vedanta
sector: Materials - Mining / Non-ferrous (routing corrected from Manufacturing master)
entity_note: Documents are Hindustan Zinc Limited (CIN L27204RJ1966PLC001208); Vedanta Ltd holds 60.71% and is treated as the parent-linkage factor.
step12_scaling_decision: A five-year projection of the credit path WAS built (Companies/vedanta/forward_model.py - rated entity HINDUSTAN ZINC LIMITED, not Vedanta Limited), with base and stress cases and the debt path DERIVED from the funding gap rather than assumed (failure mode 18). What was NOT run is the equity-research plugin's native 3-statement workbook. Reason: the company has PUBLISHED both sides of its own funding equation over exactly this window - capex of 'Rs 40,000-50,000 crore over the next five years' to lift refined metal capacity from 1.1 to 2.0 Mtpa, and an internal estimate of 'pre-growth capex free cash flow generation of Rs 55,000-65,000 crore over the next five years' (FY2025-26 integrated report). The analytical task is therefore not to build a 3-statement forecast but to test that plan, which the model does directly. On the midpoints the programme leaves about Rs 15,000 crore over five years, Rs 3,000 crore a year, for dividends - against Rs 12,253 crore actually paid in FY2025 and Rs 4,225 crore in FY2026. So the DIVIDEND, not the capex and not the zinc price, is the variable that decides the leverage path, and it is set by a board on which a 60.71% parent with its own cash needs is represented. The stress case therefore combines a commodity down-cycle with a dividend held at the FY2025 rate, because on this issuer those are correlated rather than independent, and it caps the dividend at distributable reserves - which shows Rs 7,055 crore of the stress-case distribution is not legally payable. The sector-defining metrics (mined metal volume, zinc cost of production per tonne) are explicit drivers, not narrative. Twelve opening-balance tie-outs. Recorded 01-Sep-2026.
